name: Coen Jonker
current_role: Founder & CEO, Tyme Group (Singapore-based digital banking group; TymeBank / GoTyme)
profile: Coenraad 'Coen' Jonker, a South African former corporate lawyer (CEO of law firm ENS) and Standard Bank community-banking director, co-founded Tyme in 2012 as a Deloitte spin-out with Tjaart van der Walt. After selling to Commonwealth Bank of Australia, they bought it back in 2018 with Patrice Motsepe's ARC; Tyme (South Africa, Philippines) became a unicorn in Dec 2024 with Nubank leading its raise.
interesting_fact: Tyme was named to TIME's 100 Most Influential Companies of 2025 and serves 23M customers across its digital banks.
deep_cut_fact: He was in GIBS's first-ever MBA class (2000-01), where Hernando de Soto's work on capital and access to finance sparked his interest in banking the unbanked; he had started as a lawyer at Edward Nathan in 1996.

public_contacts.value: Rachel.Freeman@tyme.com (Tyme Group media queries and interview requests)

notes: Press release names Rachel Freeman (now Chief Growth Officer) as media/interview contact.

name: Xu Shangshang
current_role: Executive Director and Chief Marketing Officer, DeepWay (深向科技)
profile: Xu Shangshang (徐上上) is a co-founder, executive director and CMO of DeepWay, the Baidu-backed electric/autonomous heavy-truck maker that filed for a Hong Kong IPO in Nov 2025. He previously held marketing roles at Wan Jun's commercial-vehicle finance group Lionbridge (狮桥) from 2013 to 2020 and followed Wan to DeepWay.
interesting_fact: DeepWay was co-founded in 2020 by Lionbridge and Baidu and holds Baidu Apollo's only 'white-box' autonomous-driving licence for commercial vehicles.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a law degree (LLB) from Anhui University of Finance and Economics.
notes: Name appears in Chinese media as 徐上上. No public contact found; route via DeepWay corporate.

name: Jeremy Gurewitz
profile: Jeremy Gurewitz started in quantitative finance, then led growth/marketing at consumer startups Imperfect Foods and Literati. In 2022 he co-founded Solace with Sara Sargent, a platform matching patients with expert healthcare advocates (ex-nurses, doctors, etc.). Solace raised a $130M Series C led by IVP in Feb 2026 at a ~$1B valuation.
interesting_fact: Solace's advocates are former doctors, nurses, pharmacists and other clinicians who help patients navigate care, second opinions and insurance.
deep_cut_fact: Before healthcare he began his career in quantitative finance and later led growth at subscription-book startup Literati, where co-founder Sara Sargent also led brand.
